title: Designed to hook you

slides.title: Attention is the product
slides.text: Free apps are not free to run. Your attention is the product being sold to advertisers, so every design choice argues for one more minute of it. The Magpie's flock sells the shiniest hooks of all.
slides.alt: A Pro technology dilemma: each side of the choice helps someone and costs someone else.

focus.cue: Video-call a relative far away, every day
Visit them once a month instead

slides.title: The hook toolkit
slides.text: Learn the toolkit by name: streaks that punish a day off, autoplay that starts the next video, endless scroll with no bottom, and notifications timed to pull you back.
slides.alt: Another technology dilemma, about machines doing tasks people used to do, and what changes when they do.

focus.cue: A watch that counts your steps
A watch that reminds you to drink water

slides.title: A design problem, not willpower
slides.text: If an app is engineered by hundreds of designers to hold you, staying is not a character test you failed. Balance is a design problem, so fix the design, not just your intentions.
slides.alt: Would you rather keep photos only on your own tablet, or keep a copy on a service someone else runs?

focus.cue: Photos only on your tablet, by design
A copy on a service someone else runs

slides.title: Match the setting to the hook
slides.text: A Defender audits the settings like Pim audits the sorting room. Match each hook to the setting that disarms it.
steps: Streaks: let one lapse on purpose
Endless scroll: set a time limit you chose
slides.alt: A second online dilemma: posting your work brings feedback, and can also show more than you meant.

focus.cue: Set the limit while you are calm
Let the setting hold it when you are not

slides.title: Your counter-toolkit
slides.text: Run the audit on pretend screens only; no real device data is collected here. Choose your limits while you are calm, and let the settings hold them when you are not.
slides.alt: A Pro technology dilemma: each side of the choice helps someone and costs someone else.

design built to steer what you do next
the next video starting by itself
an alert an app sends to pull you back

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: There is no game this time. Run the settings-audit challenge on the pretend screens with your teacher, and set one limit you chose yourself.
slides.alt: Another technology dilemma, about machines doing tasks people used to do, and what changes when they do.

talk: Which hook in the toolkit holds you longest, and which single setting change would weaken it most?
